title: Ridge penalty induced by a frozen linear transform
purpose: Compute the generalized ridge penalty (A A^T)^-1 that weight decay on trainable weights w induces on the effective coefficients beta = A w, and fit both routes to confirm they give the same coefficients. Use it to read reparameterized or overparameterized linear layers as explicit penalties.

entry_points.name: induced_penalty
entry_points.arguments: transform: k by m matrix A with full row rank (k <= m)

entry_points.name: fit_through_transform
entry_points.arguments: features: n by k; targets: n; transform: k by m; ridge > 0

entry_points.name: fit_generalized_ridge
entry_points.arguments: features: n by k; targets: n; penalty_matrix: k by k symmetric positive semidefinite; ridge > 0

assumptions: A is frozen and has full row rank, so A A^T is invertible.
Only w is trained, with the penalty ridge * ||w||^2 and squared error loss.
guarantees: The coefficients from training w equal the generalized ridge coefficients with P = (A A^T)^-1, up to rounding.
A = [I, I] gives P = I / 2; c copies of the identity give I / c; scaling A by c divides P by c^2.
A transform without full row rank raises ValueError.

known_wrong.name: penalty_is_not_left_at_full_strength
known_wrong.why: Plain ridge at the original strength ignores that duplicated columns halve the effective penalty.

limits: Dense linear algebra for small k and m (tens). Requires ridge > 0 and a full-row-rank transform; a rank-deficient A has no finite induced penalty in the missing directions. Squared error only: for other losses the penalty identity still holds but the fitted coefficients come from a different optimizer. Says nothing about generalization or which penalty is better for a task.
technique_references: Minimum-norm solution of an underdetermined linear system
